title: ADA Analytical Parameter Value Registry
description: Registry of reusable schema:PropertyValue parameter-value definitions derived from technique TAPP spreadsheets. Each $def constrains one per-dataset schema:PropertyValue entry. Detail building blocks reference these definitions via fragment $refs (schema.yaml#/$defs/<name>) so they resolve locally through the building-block register. The root only hosts $defs; it has no instantiable properties of its own.

coupledProtocolDoi.title: Coupled Protocol DOI
coupledProtocolDoi.description: Registered protocol DOI for the coupled technique named above. Provides a stable, citable link to the companion method independent of whether a dataset has been deposited. If the coupled protocol has not yet been registered, enter the DOI of a publication describing the coupled method, or "pending". Enter "None" if no coupling is planned.

coupledDatasetOrPublicationReference.title: Coupled Dataset or Publication Reference
coupledDatasetOrPublicationReference.description: DOI or other persistent identifier for the co-registered dataset or publication where both datasets are reported together. Accepts: a dedicated dataset DOI (if separately deposited), a shared dataset DOI (if co-submitted in the same package), or a publication DOI. Use "same submission" if the coupled dataset is included in this data package, or "pending" if not yet assigned. If coupling is documented through a shared sample identifier only, that information is already captured in Sample Persistent Identifier (Group 2).

sampleMass.title: Sample Mass
sampleMass.description: Mass of the sample in grams, recorded for curatorial tracking of precious or limited materials. Particularly important for meteorite, mission-returned, and other restricted samples. This is an analysis-level field: the actual sample mass depends on the specific sample being scanned, not on the protocol design.

sampleMountingMethod.title: Sample Mounting Method
sampleMountingMethod.description: Method used to mount or hold the sample on the instrument rotation stage. Mounting material should transmit X-rays at the selected voltage without dominating beam attenuation. Report the holder type, adhesive or support material, and any alignment aids used.

samplePersistentIdentifier.title: Sample Persistent Identifier
samplePersistentIdentifier.description: Globally unique, persistent identifier for the analysed sample. IGSN (International Geo Sample Number) is the recommended standard for geological and cosmochemical samples.

samplePreparationNotes.title: Sample Preparation Notes
samplePreparationNotes.description: Any preparation steps applied to the sample before scanning, including cleaning, trimming, consolidation, or drying. XCT is typically non-destructive with no surface preparation required; note any exceptions.

reconstructionSoftware.title: Reconstruction Software
reconstructionSoftware.description: Software used to reconstruct 2D projection images into a 3D CT volume, including version number. Often bundled with the instrument and proprietary to the manufacturer.

segmentationAndAnalysisSoftware.title: Segmentation and Analysis Software
segmentationAndAnalysisSoftware.description: Software used for image segmentation, phase identification, and quantitative 3D analysis after reconstruction. Report all packages used, with version numbers.

labxct_acceleratingVoltage.title: Accelerating Voltage
labxct_acceleratingVoltage.description: X-ray tube accelerating voltage in kilovolts (kV) registered by the protocol. Determines the maximum X-ray photon energy and controls penetration depth and phase contrast. Higher voltages provide greater penetration for dense or large samples; lower voltages improve contrast between low-density phases. If the voltage was varied across samples within the same protocol or session, report the full range applied (e.g., 90–115 kV). Note: some sources report this parameter as 'X keV' (maximum Bremsstrahlung photon energy) rather than 'X kV' (tube voltage). For polychromatic lab XCT, these are numerically equivalent: E_max [keV] = V [kV]. Record the value as stated in the source and add a parenthetical note if the unit used is keV.

tubeCurrent.title: Tube Current
tubeCurrent.description: X-ray tube current in microamperes (µA) registered by the protocol. Controls photon flux and therefore projection image SNR. Higher current improves SNR but increases thermal loading on the source and may increase focal spot size. If the current was varied across samples within the same protocol or session, report the full range applied (e.g., 65–115 µA).

xRayPower.title: X-ray Power
xRayPower.description: X-ray tube power in watts (W) registered by the protocol. Derivable as voltage (kV) × current (mA) = kV × µA / 1000. Power constrains the achievable focal spot size for microfocal tubes: higher power requires a larger focal spot, trading spatial resolution for SNR. Retained as a standalone field because it is routinely reported in the literature and directly constrains instrument operating limits. If power was varied across samples within the session, report the full range applied (e.g., 7–13 W).

xRayPreFilter.title: X-ray Pre-filter
xRayPreFilter.description: Material and thickness of the beam-hardening filter placed between the X-ray source and the sample. Hardens the beam by attenuating low-energy photons, reducing beam hardening artifacts and improving CT number stability across the sample. Both filter material and thickness must be reported. Instrument-proprietary filter codes should be decoded where possible.

sourceToObjectDistance.title: Source-to-Object Distance (SOD)
sourceToObjectDistance.description: Distance from the X-ray source focal spot to the centre of the sample rotation axis, in mm, as registered by the protocol. Together with SDD, determines geometric magnification (M = SDD/SOD). Shorter SOD increases magnification and reduces voxel size.

sourceToDetectorDistance.title: Source-to-Detector Distance (SDD)
sourceToDetectorDistance.description: Distance from the X-ray source focal spot to the detector surface, in mm, as registered by the protocol. Together with SOD, determines geometric magnification M = SDD/SOD. Voxel size ≈ detector pixel size / M (before binning; divide additionally by optical objective for Versa-class systems).

voxelSize.title: Voxel Size
voxelSize.description: Isotropic voxel edge length of the reconstructed 3D volume in micrometres. The protocol registers the target voxel size, set based on the minimum feature size to be resolved (target voxel size ≤ ~1/3 of the minimum resolvable feature size). At analysis level, record the achieved voxel size as reported by the reconstruction software, which may differ slightly from the target due to final geometric calibration.

rotationRange.title: Rotation Range
rotationRange.description: Total angular range over which projection images are acquired, in degrees. Full 360° rotation is standard for cone-beam lab XCT. 180° rotation (half-scan) is sometimes used for faster acquisition but may introduce additional artifacts.

numberOfProjections.title: Number of Projections
numberOfProjections.description: Total number of equally-spaced projection images acquired over the full rotation range. More projections improve reconstruction quality by reducing under-sampling streak artifacts but increase scan time. For Mode B (multi-volume stitching), this is the number per sub-volume.

rotationStepSize.title: Rotation Step Size
rotationStepSize.description: Angular increment between successive projection images, in degrees. Equal to Rotation Range divided by Number of Projections when both are reported; however, some sources report step size as the primary rotation parameter without stating the total number of projections explicitly. Finer step sizes improve angular sampling and reduce streak artifacts at the cost of longer scan time.

exposureTimePerProjection.title: Exposure Time per Projection
exposureTimePerProjection.description: Duration of X-ray exposure for each individual projection image frame, in seconds, as registered by the protocol. Set as a deliberate choice for the target sample type and voxel size: longer exposures increase SNR at the cost of total scan time. May be adjusted within protocol-allowed bounds for samples that are unusually dense or unusually transparent. If the exposure time was varied across samples within the same protocol or session, report the full range applied (e.g., 0.5–2 s).

framesAveragedPerProjection.title: Frames Averaged per Projection
framesAveragedPerProjection.description: Number of individual detector frames acquired and averaged to produce each saved projection image, as registered by the protocol. Frame averaging reduces random electronic noise. The effective exposure per projection = exposure time per frame × frames averaged.

detectorBinning.title: Detector Binning
detectorBinning.description: Detector pixel binning factor applied during acquisition. Binning combines adjacent pixels (e.g., 2×2 combines 4 pixels into one), reducing effective resolution while increasing per-pixel SNR and reducing file size. 1×1 indicates no binning.

flatFieldCorrection.title: Flat Field Correction
flatFieldCorrection.description: Whether dark-field (detector read with X-ray source off; electronic noise baseline) and bright-field (source on, no sample; gain calibration) reference images are acquired and applied to normalize detector response before reconstruction. Standard practice in all quantitative lab XCT;.

rotationMode.title: Rotation Mode
rotationMode.description: Whether projection images are acquired during continuous sample rotation (faster; may introduce slight motion blur at high rotation speeds) or at discrete step positions with the stage stationary during each exposure (stop-and-shoot; eliminates motion blur). Continuous rotation has been associated with sub-volume rotational mismatch artifacts in multi-volume stitching workflows (Eckley et al. 2025).

totalScanDuration.title: Total Scan Duration
totalScanDuration.description: Total elapsed time for the complete XCT acquisition, from the start of the first projection to the end of the last. For multi-volume acquisitions, this is the combined scan time across all sub-volumes (not including setup or reconstruction time). Useful for assessing beam stability and sample integrity concerns over long scans.

reconstructionConvolutionFilter.title: Reconstruction Convolution Filter
reconstructionConvolutionFilter.description: Convolution (apodization) filter kernel applied during back-projection reconstruction. Sharper filters (Ram-Lak) enhance edge definition but amplify high-frequency noise; smoother filters (Hann, Hamming) reduce noise at the cost of edge sharpness. The choice represents a deliberate protocol-level tradeoff.

beamHardeningCorrectionParameter.title: Beam Hardening Correction Parameter
beamHardeningCorrectionParameter.description: Numerical value or setting applied in the software beam hardening correction algorithm for this specific analysis. May be tuned empirically per material type or per scan session. Analysis-level companion to Beam Hardening Correction Method.

ringArtifactCorrectionMethod.title: Ring Artifact Correction Method
ringArtifactCorrectionMethod.description: Protocol specification for how ring artifacts are handled. Ring artifacts appear as concentric circular bands centred on the rotation axis and arise from defective or miscalibrated detector pixels. Method is the protocol-level specification; whether correction was applied and its outcome are recorded at analysis level in Group 6.

outputDataFormat.title: Output Data Format
outputDataFormat.description: File format of the reconstructed CT volume as output by the reconstruction software. Bit depth is recorded separately in Output Bit Depth.

ctNumberCalibration.title: CT Number Calibration
ctNumberCalibration.description: Whether the raw CT grayscale values have been calibrated to physically meaningful units using reference materials. Calibrated CT numbers enable cross-instrument and cross-session comparison and support phase identification by comparison to calculated linear attenuation coefficient (LAC) values (e.g., using MuCalc; Hanna & Ketcham 2017). Uncalibrated grayscale values are instrument- and session-specific.

segmentationMethod.title: Segmentation Method
segmentationMethod.description: General approach used to separate distinct phases or features in the reconstructed CT volume. The method must be reported for any quantitative result to be reproducible.

segmentationThresholdValuesOrCriteria.title: Segmentation Threshold Values or Criteria
segmentationThresholdValuesOrCriteria.description: Specific CT number range(s) or quantitative criteria used to define each segmented phase or feature. Documenting these values enables reproducibility assessment and cross-study comparison. For LAC-calibrated datasets, report values in cm⁻¹.

phaseIdentificationMethod.title: Phase Identification Method
phaseIdentificationMethod.description: Method used to assign reconstructed CT number ranges to specific mineral phases or material types. Approaches include comparison to calculated linear attenuation coefficients (LAC), cross-validation with independent analytical techniques, or empirical calibration.

voiSelectionCriteria.title: VOI Selection Criteria
voiSelectionCriteria.description: Protocol-level rules specifying how the Volume of Interest (VOI) is to be defined for quantitative analysis. Common criteria exclude cone-beam artifact zones at sample edges, beam hardening halos near dense inclusions, and sample holder signal. The actual VOI applied in a specific analysis is recorded separately at analysis level.

subVolumeStitchingAndRegistrationMethod.title: Sub-volume Stitching and Registration Method
subVolumeStitchingAndRegistrationMethod.description: Method used to register adjacent sub-volume datasets to each other and stitch them into a single continuous 3D volume. Report the alignment strategy (manual, automated, fiducial-based), the software used, and any correction steps applied. Note: rotational mismatch artifacts have been identified in continuous-rotation acquisitions (~0.35° misalignment in Eckley et al. 2025); their correction via raw projection re-alignment should be documented here.

outputBitDepth.title: Output Bit Depth
outputBitDepth.description: Bit depth of the reconstructed 3D volume (number of bits used to encode each voxel's grayscale value). Common values are 8-bit (256 gray levels), 16-bit (65,536 gray levels), or 32-bit floating point. Bit depth affects the dynamic range available for phase segmentation and quantitative attenuation analysis. The protocol may specify a required output bit depth if downstream analysis workflows depend on a consistent grayscale range; the analyst confirms or adjusts at analysis time.

spatialResolution.title: Spatial Resolution
spatialResolution.description: Effective spatial resolution of the reconstructed CT volume, which typically differs from (and is coarser than) the voxel size due to the detector point spread function (PSF), geometric unsharpness, and the reconstruction filter. The Nyquist limit sets a theoretical floor at 2× the voxel size. Formal measurement uses the PSF method described in Ketcham & Hildebrandt (2014) or the modulation transfer function (MTF); resolution can also be reported per ASTM E1441-11. When formal measurement is unavailable, an estimate based on acquisition geometry (e.g., the Brenner-Weiss formula) or a stated multiple of the voxel size may be recorded. Report the value in µm along with the method used to determine or estimate it.

beamHardeningArtifactAssessment.title: Beam Hardening Artifact Assessment
beamHardeningArtifactAssessment.description: Assessment of whether residual beam hardening (cupping artifact) is present in the reconstructed volume after any corrections applied during reconstruction. Beam hardening in polychromatic lab XCT produces a characteristic darker interior and brighter edges in the reconstructed CT number profile, even in compositionally uniform material. Record whether this artifact is detectable in the final dataset, what correction or mitigation was applied (e.g., linearisation, pre-filtering, iterative correction), and whether any residual effect influences the analysis region.

ringArtifactSeverityAndCorrectionOutcome.title: Ring Artifact Severity and Correction Outcome
ringArtifactSeverityAndCorrectionOutcome.description: Assessment of whether ring artifacts — concentric rings centred on the rotation axis arising from differential sensitivity or gain drift among detector elements — were present and whether correction was effective. Note that ring correction algorithms modify image intensity in narrow annular bands; in samples containing linear geological features oriented tangentially to the rotation axis, ring correction can alter or introduce spurious linear features in those orientations. Record whether rings were present, whether correction was applied, and whether any residual rings or correction artifacts fall within the analysis volume of interest.

schema:name.const: Ring Artifact Severity and Correction Outcome

metalStreakArtifactAssessment.title: Metal Streak Artifact Assessment
metalStreakArtifactAssessment.description: Assessment of whether high-density inclusions (FeNi metal, platinum-group minerals, dense oxides, or other high-Z phases) produce streak or starburst artifacts in the reconstructed volume. Common forms include radial starburst streaks from high-Z inclusions and shadowing (anomalously low CT number) in beam-shadow regions behind dense phases. Record which artifact type(s) are present, their spatial extent, and any exclusion zones or correction steps applied.

partialVolumeEffectCriteria.title: Partial Volume Effect Criteria
partialVolumeEffectCriteria.description: Protocol-level specification of how partial volume effects (PVE) are managed in quantitative analysis. PVE produces intermediate CT numbers at phase boundaries and at the surfaces of small features, because each voxel integrates the attenuation of all material within its volume. PVE correction can be implemented via PSF-based deconvolution tools such as Blob3D. Record the minimum feature size criterion adopted for the protocol (in voxels or µm), the treatment of boundary voxels in modal abundance or size distribution calculations, and whether PVE correction is required or optional.

partialVolumeEffectAssessment.title: Partial Volume Effect Assessment
partialVolumeEffectAssessment.description: Analysis-level record of PVE severity and how it was handled in this specific analysis. Documents the minimum feature size relative to the voxel size, the fraction of the feature population affected, and any PVE correction method applied (e.g., PSF-based deconvolution via Blob3D).

minimumResolvableFeatureSize.title: Minimum Resolvable Feature Size
minimumResolvableFeatureSize.description: Smallest feature reliably detected and quantified in this analysis at the achieved voxel size and SNR. The practical detection limit is determined jointly by voxel size, effective spatial resolution (PSF), and image contrast. Per Withers et al. (2021), a feature must span at least 3 voxels to be positively identified, and at least 10 voxels for reliable shape and volume characterisation. Report the minimum feature size threshold applied in quantitative analysis and the basis for that value (e.g., SNR-limited, PVE-limited, or analyst-defined).

signalToNoiseRatio.title: Signal-to-Noise Ratio
signalToNoiseRatio.description: Quantitative measure of image quality in the reconstructed CT volume. Typically calculated as the mean CT number divided by the standard deviation of CT number in a homogeneous reference region (e.g., an inclusion-free zone of the matrix). SNR is controlled by photon flux (source power, exposure time, number of projections) and sample attenuation. Record the measured value and the region used for measurement, or note if SNR was not formally measured.

crossValidationProtocolRequirement.title: Cross-Validation Protocol Requirement
crossValidationProtocolRequirement.description: Protocol-level specification of what independent analytical validation is required to confirm CT segmentation results, phase identification, or quantitative measurements. Cross-validation is relevant where CT grey-values alone cannot uniquely distinguish phases with similar attenuation coefficients. Common approaches include BSE imaging, SEM-EDS or EPMA modal analysis, He pycnometry for bulk porosity, and Raman or SIMS phase mapping. Record the required validation method(s) and the sampling fraction (e.g., every sample, one per session, or a representative subset).

crossValidationOutcome.title: Cross-Validation Outcome
crossValidationOutcome.description: Analysis-level record of what independent validation was performed and its result. Report the validation method(s) used, the quantitative agreement achieved (e.g., relative difference in modal abundance, porosity), and any discrepancies and their likely causes. Where BSE imaging is the validation method, note that BSE provides a 2D section while CT provides a 3D volume.

xRayTubeAnodeMaterial.title: X-ray Tube Anode Material
xRayTubeAnodeMaterial.description: Material of the X-ray tube anode (target). Determines the characteristic line energies superimposed on the bremsstrahlung continuum, which can affect phase contrast at specific energies. Multi-metal anodes (e.g., W/Mo/Cu) extend the usable energy range.

detectorArraySize.title: Detector Array Size
detectorArraySize.description: Number of pixels in the detector array (width × height). Combined with detector pixel size and geometric magnification, determines the field of view.

detectorPixelSize.title: Detector Pixel Size
detectorPixelSize.description: Physical size of a single pixel on the detector in micrometres. This is a fixed hardware property of the detector array, distinct from the reconstructed voxel size (which depends on geometric magnification and binning).

opticalObjective.title: Optical Objective
opticalObjective.description: Optical magnification objective installed between the scintillator and CCD/CMOS detector. Applies only to instruments using optical magnification (e.g., Zeiss Xradia Versa series). For systems using only geometric magnification, report "Not applicable".

tem_coupledProtocolDoi.title: Coupled Protocol DOI
tem_coupledProtocolDoi.description: DOI of the registered protocol for the coupled technique.

tem_coupledDatasetOrPublicationReference.title: Coupled Dataset or Publication Reference
tem_coupledDatasetOrPublicationReference.description: DOI of the dataset or publication containing the coupled technique data.

tem_samplePersistentIdentifier.title: Sample Persistent Identifier
tem_samplePersistentIdentifier.description: Persistent identifier (e.g., IGSN) for the sample analyzed.

tem_acceleratingVoltage.title: Accelerating Voltage
tem_acceleratingVoltage.description: Electron beam accelerating voltage in kilovolts (kV). For beam-sensitive materials (organic matter, phyllosilicates), 60–80 kV may be used to stay below the displacement threshold for C, N, O, and S. The protocol specifies the standard operating voltage; analysts record and justify deviations.

analyticalMode.title: Analytical Sub-mode
analyticalMode.description: Sub-mode(s) of imaging or diffraction performed under this protocol. TEM Imaging options: BF-TEM, DF-TEM, HRTEM, EFTEM. STEM Imaging options: HAADF, ABF, BF-STEM, ADF, MAADF. Electron Diffraction options: SAED, CBED, Nanobeam diffraction, Precession ED, 4D-STEM. Multiple values apply when the protocol covers more than one sub-mode within a given analytical mode.

temObjectiveAperture.title: TEM Objective Aperture
temObjectiveAperture.description: Objective aperture diameter used to select the imaging beam condition in TEM mode. In BF-TEM, a small aperture blocks diffracted beams to enhance mass-thickness contrast; in DF-TEM, the aperture is displaced to select a specific diffracted beam; in HRTEM, no aperture is typically used.

eftemEnergyWindow.title: EFTEM Energy Window
eftemEnergyWindow.description: Energy window(s) used for EFTEM elemental mapping: center energy, width, and acquisition method (three-window or jump-ratio).

haadfCollectionAngles.title: HAADF Collection Angles
haadfCollectionAngles.description: Inner and outer collection angles of the HAADF detector in milliradians (mrad). The inner angle determines the boundary between diffracted and thermally diffuse scattered electrons; larger inner angles yield stronger Z-contrast and reduced Bragg contrast.

stemProbeDiameter.title: STEM Probe Diameter
stemProbeDiameter.description: Nominal or measured diameter of the focused electron probe at the sample, reported in nm. Serves as a direct spatial resolution proxy for STEM imaging and STEM-EDS/EELS analysis. Related to, but distinct from, Convergence Semi-Angle: the two quantities are connected via aberration coefficients, defocus, and probe current, which are not always published. Report whichever is known; if both are known, report both fields.

stemProbeCurrent.title: STEM Probe Current
stemProbeCurrent.description: Probe current in picoamperes (pA) or nanoamperes (nA). Higher current improves EDS/EELS signal but increases beam damage risk, especially for organic matter and hydrous minerals.

stemDwellTimePerPixel.title: STEM Dwell Time per Pixel
stemDwellTimePerPixel.description: Time spent acquiring signal at each pixel during STEM scanning in milliseconds. Longer dwell improves signal-to-noise but increases total specimen dose; for dose-sensitive materials, minimize dwell and compensate with frame averaging.

stemScanDimensions.title: STEM Scan Dimensions
stemScanDimensions.description: Number of pixels in the STEM scan frame (X × Y pixels). Combined with calibrated pixel size, defines the field of view.

stemFrameAveraging.title: STEM Frame Averaging
stemFrameAveraging.description: Number of frames averaged (with drift correction if applicable) to produce the final STEM image. Averaging reduces noise while limiting per-frame dose.

cameraLength.title: Camera Length
cameraLength.description: Nominal camera length in millimeters used for diffraction pattern acquisition. Controls the mapping between reciprocal-space scattering angle and detector position; must be calibrated to convert pixel distances to d-spacings. In STEM mode, also sets HAADF/ABF detector collection angles.

selectedAreaApertureSize.title: Selected-Area Aperture Size
selectedAreaApertureSize.description: Diameter of the selected-area aperture used in SAED mode, defining the specimen region that contributes to the diffraction pattern.

precessionAngle.title: Precession Angle
precessionAngle.description: Precession semi-angle in degrees for precession electron diffraction (PED). Hollow-cone illumination reduces dynamical diffraction effects and produces more kinematical-like intensities. Not applicable to SAED, CBED, or standard 4D-STEM.

4dStemScanGridAndArea.title: 4D-STEM Scan Grid and Area
4dStemScanGridAndArea.description: Number of probe positions in the 4D-STEM dataset (scan pixels × scan pixels) and the physical area covered. Probe step size is the physical area divided by scan pixel count.

4dStemDwellTimePerProbePosition.title: 4D-STEM Dwell Time per Probe Position
4dStemDwellTimePerProbePosition.description: Time spent acquiring each diffraction pattern in the 4D-STEM dataset in milliseconds. Longer dwell improves signal-to-noise for weakly diffracting phases (e.g., smectite 001 reflection at ~1.24 nm) but increases total specimen dose; risk of beam damage to phyllosilicates and organic matter must be balanced against data quality.

diffractionCameraLengthCalibrationMethod.title: Diffraction Camera Length Calibration Method
diffractionCameraLengthCalibrationMethod.description: Method used to calibrate the camera length constant and convert pixel distances in diffraction patterns to d-spacings or reciprocal lattice vectors.

edsLiveTimePerPointOrPixel.title: EDS Live Time per Point or Pixel
edsLiveTimePerPointOrPixel.description: EDS spectral acquisition live time per analysis point (point/line mode) or per pixel (spectrum image) in seconds. Also referred to as "EDS Acquisition Time" in EPMA and some SEM-EDS contexts, where the per-pixel distinction is less relevant.

schema:name.const: EDS Live Time per Point or Pixel

edsEnergyRange.title: EDS Energy Range
edsEnergyRange.description: Energy range of EDS spectrum acquisition in keV.

eelsEdges.title: EELS Edges
eelsEdges.description: Ionization edge(s) acquired by EELS, specified by element symbol and edge label (e.g., Fe L2,3; O K). Provides the EELS-specific counterpart to the Analyte field: while Analyte lists elements, EELS Edges documents which ionization edges were used and their approximate energy loss positions. The protocol registers the full intended edge suite; analysts confirm or narrow this list at analysis time.

eelsAcquisitionTimePerSpectrum.title: EELS Acquisition Time per Spectrum
eelsAcquisitionTimePerSpectrum.description: Exposure time per individual EELS spectrum (or per pixel for spectrum images) in seconds.

eelsEnergyLossRange.title: EELS Energy Loss Range
eelsEnergyLossRange.description: Energy loss range acquired, defined by onset energy and width in eV. The protocol documents the target range for the registered analyte edges; analysts record the actual range acquired.

eelsBackgroundSubtractionMethod.title: EELS Background Subtraction Method
eelsBackgroundSubtractionMethod.description: Method used to subtract the background beneath the ionization edge of interest to extract the net edge signal.

eelsPluralScatteringCorrection.title: EELS Plural Scattering Correction
eelsPluralScatteringCorrection.description: Method applied to correct for multiple inelastic scattering events (plural scattering) that broaden edge fine structure. Critical for specimens thicker than ~0.5 inelastic mean free paths.

imageProcessingMethodsApplied.title: Image Processing Methods Applied
imageProcessingMethodsApplied.description: Image processing steps applied to TEM or STEM images during or after acquisition. Non-linear processing steps that could affect quantitative interpretation should be documented explicitly.

specimenThicknessDeterminationMethod.title: Specimen Thickness Determination Method
specimenThicknessDeterminationMethod.description: Method used to estimate TEM foil thickness. Required for EELS quantification (log-ratio) and for assessing multiple-scattering severity.

edsCalibrationStandard.title: EDS Calibration Standard(s)
edsCalibrationStandard.description: Reference material(s) used to validate EDS quantification or determine experimental k-factors or zeta-factors. TEM-EDS is less standardized than EPMA; many protocols rely on manufacturer k-factors without external calibration.

eelsEnergyCalibration.title: EELS Energy Calibration
eelsEnergyCalibration.description: Method and reference used to calibrate the EELS energy axis. Accurate calibration is required for ELNES edge identification, chemical-state analysis, and inter-lab comparability.

diffractionCalibrationReference.title: Diffraction Calibration Reference
diffractionCalibrationReference.description: Reference material or internal standard used to calibrate the electron diffraction camera constant (camera length × electron wavelength), enabling conversion of pixel distances to d-spacings.

edsCountingStatisticsAccumulationCriteri.title: EDS Counting Statistics / Accumulation Criterion
edsCountingStatisticsAccumulationCriteri.description: Quality criterion used to determine when sufficient EDS signal has been accumulated for a given pixel or point, in lieu of or in addition to a fixed live time. Expressed as a target relative uncertainty on major-element peak counts achieved by accumulating successive scan frames (e.g., "1% counting statistics on major elements"; ">10% counting statistics"). Distinct from EDS Live Time per Point or Pixel, which records a fixed-duration setting.

eelsEnergyDispersion.title: EELS Energy Dispersion
eelsEnergyDispersion.description: Energy dispersion of the EELS spectrometer in eV per channel. Controls the energy range acquired per readout and the effective energy resolution trade-off.

eelsEnergyResolution.title: EELS Energy Resolution
eelsEnergyResolution.description: Full-width at half-maximum (FWHM) of the zero-loss peak in eV, measured at operating conditions. Reflects combined electron source energy spread and monochromator effect (if active). Critical for ELNES fine-structure interpretation.

4dStemOrientationMappingMethod.title: 4D-STEM Orientation Mapping Method
4dStemOrientationMappingMethod.description: Algorithm, software module, and reference crystal structure database used for automated crystal orientation mapping (ACOM) from 4D-STEM datasets.

tem_edsSpectralProcessingType.title: EDS Spectral Processing Type
tem_edsSpectralProcessingType.description: Method used to process EDS spectra and extract net peak intensities from raw spectral data. Applied before quantification (EDS Quantification Method). Common approaches include background fitting and subtraction followed by peak integration, and filter fit or Gaussian deconvolution for overlapping peaks.

semImaging_coupledProtocolDoi.title: Coupled Protocol DOI
semImaging_coupledProtocolDoi.description: DOI of the registered protocol for the coupled technique.

semImaging_coupledDatasetOrPublicationRe.title: Coupled Dataset or Publication Reference
semImaging_coupledDatasetOrPublicationRe.description: DOI of the dataset or publication containing the coupled technique data. If coupling is documented only through a shared sample IGSN, this field may be 'None'.

semImaging_samplePersistentIdentifier.title: Sample Persistent Identifier
semImaging_samplePersistentIdentifier.description: Persistent identifier (e.g., IGSN) for the sample analyzed.

semImaging_acceleratingVoltage.title: Accelerating Voltage
semImaging_acceleratingVoltage.description: Electron beam accelerating voltage in kilovolts. Affects X-ray generation depth (EDS/WDS), EBSD pattern quality, imaging resolution, and beam penetration. Low voltages (1-5 kV) improve surface sensitivity and reduce beam damage; high voltages (15-20 kV) improve X-ray generation for quantitative analysis.

semImaging_beamCurrent.title: Beam Current
semImaging_beamCurrent.description: Electron beam probe current. Higher current improves signal-to-noise for X-ray analysis (EDS/WDS, EBSD) and CL but may increase beam damage and reduce spatial resolution. Express in nA; for sub-nA values use decimal notation (e.g., 0.4 nA).

workingDistance.title: Working Distance
workingDistance.description: Distance between the objective lens pole piece and the specimen surface in millimetres. Affects spatial resolution, depth of focus, EDS X-ray take-off angle, and EBSD geometry.

chamberPressure.title: Chamber Pressure
chamberPressure.description: Chamber pressure and gas type during analysis. Required for variable pressure (VP-SEM) and environmental SEM (ESEM) modes. Report value and unit (Pa or Torr) and gas composition. Use 'None' for standard high-vacuum operation.

dwellTimePerPixel.title: Dwell Time per Pixel
dwellTimePerPixel.description: Time the electron beam dwells on each pixel during raster scanning (imaging modes) or on each step position during compositional mapping (EDS and WDS mapping modes), in microseconds or milliseconds. Longer dwell time improves signal-to-noise and counting statistics but increases total dose and can cause beam damage or contamination on sensitive materials. For WDS mapping, the dwell time is per spectrometer per pixel.

clIntegrationTime.title: CL Integration Time
clIntegrationTime.description: Acquisition time per pixel (hyperspectral map mode) or per spectrum (spectral point mode), in ms or s. Longer integration improves signal-to-noise but increases beam dose and acquisition time.

stepSize.title: EBSD Step Size
stepSize.description: Distance between adjacent EBSD measurement points in the map in nm or µm. Must be smaller than the smallest grain of interest to resolve grain boundary positions and intragrain orientation gradients.

frameTime.title: EBSD Frame Time
frameTime.description: Acquisition time per EBSD diffraction pattern frame in milliseconds. Longer frame time improves pattern quality and indexing rate but increases total acquisition time.

phaseList.title: EBSD Phase List
phaseList.description: Mineral phases included in the EBSD reference pattern library for this protocol. The protocol specifies the expected phase suite for the target material; analysts may add phases for specific sample compositions.

crystalStructureDatabase.title: Crystal Structure Database
crystalStructureDatabase.description: Crystal structure database used for EBSD phase identification and Kikuchi pattern simulation.

patternQualityThreshold.title: EBSD Pattern Quality Threshold
patternQualityThreshold.description: Minimum pattern quality or confidence index threshold applied during EBSD data processing to exclude unreliably indexed points from orientation maps. Include metric name and threshold value.

clWavelengthCalibrationReference.title: CL Wavelength Calibration Reference
clWavelengthCalibrationReference.description: Reference light source or standard material used to calibrate the wavelength axis of the CL spectrometer. Required for quantitative spectral CL and hyperspectral mapping.

clDetectorConfiguration.title: CL Detector Configuration
clDetectorConfiguration.description: CL detector type, manufacturer, model, collection optics (e.g., parabolic mirror, elliptical mirror, light guide), and spectral detection configuration (PMT for panchromatic, CCD/EMCCD for spectral, multi-channel for pseudo-color CL).

clWavelengthRange.title: CL Grating
clWavelengthRange.description: Diffraction grating specification for spectral or hyperspectral CL acquisition, including groove density and blaze wavelength. Not applicable to panchromatic-only acquisition.

semFibsem_coupledProtocolDoi.title: Coupled Protocol DOI
semFibsem_coupledProtocolDoi.description: DOI of the registered protocol for the coupled technique.

semFibsem_coupledDatasetOrPublicationRef.title: Coupled Dataset or Publication Reference
semFibsem_coupledDatasetOrPublicationRef.description: DOI of the dataset or publication containing the coupled technique data. If coupling is documented only through a shared sample IGSN, this field may be 'None'.

semFibsem_samplePersistentIdentifier.title: Sample Persistent Identifier
semFibsem_samplePersistentIdentifier.description: Persistent identifier (e.g., IGSN) for the sample analyzed.

semFibsem_acceleratingVoltage.title: Accelerating Voltage
semFibsem_acceleratingVoltage.description: Electron beam accelerating voltage in kilovolts. Affects X-ray generation depth (EDS/WDS), EBSD pattern quality, imaging resolution, and beam penetration. Low voltages (1-5 kV) improve surface sensitivity and reduce beam damage; high voltages (15-20 kV) improve X-ray generation for quantitative analysis.

semFibsem_beamCurrent.title: Beam Current
semFibsem_beamCurrent.description: Electron beam probe current. Higher current improves signal-to-noise for X-ray analysis (EDS/WDS, EBSD) and CL but may increase beam damage and reduce spatial resolution. Express in nA; for sub-nA values use decimal notation (e.g., 0.4 nA).

semFibsem_workingDistance.title: Working Distance
semFibsem_workingDistance.description: Distance between the objective lens pole piece and the specimen surface in millimetres. Affects spatial resolution, depth of focus, EDS X-ray take-off angle, and EBSD geometry.

semFibsem_dwellTimePerPixel.title: Dwell Time per Pixel
semFibsem_dwellTimePerPixel.description: Time the electron beam dwells on each pixel during raster scanning (imaging modes) or on each step position during compositional mapping (EDS and WDS mapping modes), in microseconds or milliseconds. Longer dwell time improves signal-to-noise and counting statistics but increases total dose and can cause beam damage or contamination on sensitive materials. For WDS mapping, the dwell time is per spectrometer per pixel.

protectiveCoatingDeposition.title: Protective Coating Deposition
protectiveCoatingDeposition.description: Type and deposition conditions of the protective coating applied to the sample surface before FIB milling. E-beam deposition causes less surface damage than ion-beam deposition and should be applied as the initial layer. Typical coatings: platinum (Pt) or carbon (C). State material, deposition method, beam conditions, and approximate thickness.

coarseMillingConditions.title: Coarse Milling Conditions
coarseMillingConditions.description: Ion beam voltage and current used for bulk material removal during FIB milling. For TEM specimen preparation: bulk trenching to isolate the lamella and intermediate thinning. For 3D tomography: face preparation and initial slice removal.

finePolishingConditions.title: Fine Polishing Conditions
finePolishingConditions.description: Ion beam voltage and current for final thinning and surface polishing of the TEM lamella. Low-voltage polishing (2 kV or below) minimises Ga implantation depth, surface amorphisation, and curtaining artifacts.

targetFoilThickness.title: Target Foil Thickness
targetFoilThickness.description: Target thickness of the electron-transparent TEM lamella after final FIB polishing, in nanometres. Actual thickness may differ from target. Typical range: 50-150 nm for standard TEM/STEM; 200-600 nm for XANES or tomography sections.

ionMillingConditions.title: Ion Milling Conditions (3D Tomography)
ionMillingConditions.description: Ion beam voltage and current used to mill each slice during FIB-SEM serial sectioning. These parameters determine material removal rate per slice and exposed surface quality.

sliceThickness.title: Slice Thickness
sliceThickness.description: Thickness of each FIB-milled slice during serial sectioning in nanometres. Controls the Z-axis resolution of the 3D reconstruction.

laicpms_coupledProtocolDoi.title: Coupled Protocol DOI
laicpms_coupledProtocolDoi.description: Registered protocol DOI for the coupled technique named above. Provides a stable, citable link to the companion method independent of whether a dataset has been deposited. If the coupled protocol has not yet been registered, enter the DOI of a publication describing the coupled method, or "pending". Enter "None" if no coupling is planned.

laicpms_coupledDatasetOrPublicationRefer.title: Coupled Dataset or Publication Reference
laicpms_coupledDatasetOrPublicationRefer.description: DOI or other persistent identifier for the co-registered dataset or publication where both datasets are reported together. Accepts: a dedicated dataset DOI (if separately deposited), a shared dataset DOI (if co-submitted in the same package), or a publication DOI. Use "same submission" if the coupled dataset is included in this data package, or "pending" if not yet assigned. If coupling is documented through a shared sample identifier only, that information is already captured in Sample Persistent Identifier (Group 2).

laicpms_samplePersistentIdentifier.title: Sample Persistent Identifier
laicpms_samplePersistentIdentifier.description: Globally unique, persistent identifier for the analysed sample. IGSN (International Geo Sample Number) is the recommended standard for geological and cosmochemical samples, as used by Astromat, EarthChem, and SESAR.

fusionFluxAndDilutionRatio.title: Fusion Flux and Dilution Ratio
fusionFluxAndDilutionRatio.description: For protocols using fused glass, the flux type and sample:flux dilution ratio used to prepare the analytical glass.

preAblationSurfaceTreatment.title: Pre-Ablation Surface Treatment
preAblationSurfaceTreatment.description: Protocol applied immediately before each analysis to remove surface contamination or condition the sample surface. Distinct from general sample preparation. For spot analysis, pre-ablation pulses are discarded before signal acquisition begins. For mapping, this step is typically omitted as the large area ablated averages out surface effects.

instrumentIdentifier.title: Instrument Serial Number or Lab Identifier
instrumentIdentifier.description: Serial number or laboratory-internal identifier for the specific instrument unit. Supports traceability to instrument service records.

schema:name.const: Instrument Serial Number or Lab Identifier

torchDepth.title: Torch Depth
torchDepth.description: Distance between the load coil and the sampling cone tip (mm), also called injector depth or torch position depending on the instrument manufacturer. Affects ion transmission efficiency, oxide formation, and doubly-charged species production. The protocol specifies a target value optimised during initial setup; the analyst confirms or fine-adjusts during session tuning.

massResolutionSetting.title: Mass Resolution Setting
massResolutionSetting.description: Operating mass resolution of the mass analyser. For quadrupole instruments this is fixed at unit resolution by instrument design. For sector-field instruments the analyst selects low, medium, or high resolution to balance sensitivity against spectral interference suppression.

spotGeometry.title: Laser Spot Geometry
spotGeometry.description: Shape and dimensions of the laser ablation spot in micrometres registered by the protocol. For circular spots, report diameter; for square or rectangular spots, report width × length. The protocol registers the typical geometry; analysts may adjust within protocol-allowed range.

laserEnergy.title: Laser Energy
laserEnergy.description: Laser pulse energy in millijoules as set at the laser output or measured at the sample surface. Less commonly reported than fluence because it does not account for spot area. Report only when the system displays energy directly. Laser fluence (J cm⁻²) is the preferred quantity and is captured in Default Laser Fluence.

laserFluence.title: Laser Fluence (Energy Density)
laserFluence.description: Laser pulse energy per unit area at the sample surface in J cm⁻², as registered by the protocol. Fluence is the physically meaningful quantity controlling ablation rate, crater morphology, elemental fractionation, and particle size distribution. If the system reports only as % of maximum output, include that value and note the system maximum where known.

laserRepetitionRate.title: Laser Repetition Rate
laserRepetitionRate.description: Laser pulse repetition rate in hertz registered by the protocol. For mapping methods, repetition rate together with scan speed and spot size determines pixel size and spatial resolution. Analysts may adjust within protocol-allowed bounds.

ablationSpotDuration.title: Ablation Duration per Spot
ablationSpotDuration.description: Total on-sample ablation (signal acquisition) time per individual spot in seconds, as set in the acquisition method. This is a protocol-level parameter for spot analysis: it reflects the deliberate trade-off between signal accumulation (longer = lower LOD), sample consumption, and session throughput. For transect analysis, the equivalent protocol-level parameter is scan speed (captured in Transect Rate, Mapping Rate or Step Size). For mapping analysis, total acquisition time is sample-area-dependent and therefore analysis-level, not captured here.

transectOrMappingRateOrStepSize.title: Transect Rate, Mapping Rate or Step Size
transectOrMappingRateOrStepSize.description: For continuous line scan (transect) and raster mapping: the stage translation speed in µm s⁻¹. This is the protocol-level parameter that, together with spot size and repetition rate, determines spatial resolution along the scan direction. For mapping, the mapping rate (mm² h⁻¹) may be reported as an alternative when scan speed is session-variable. For stepped line profiles: the distance between successive spot positions in µm.

schema:name.const: Transect Rate, Mapping Rate or Step Size

rasterLineSpacing.title: Raster Line Spacing (Mapping Only)
rasterLineSpacing.description: Distance between adjacent raster lines in a 2D elemental map, measured perpendicular to the scan direction, in micrometres. Together with spot size, this determines whether adjacent lines are contiguous (line spacing = spot size), overlapping (line spacing < spot size), or have gaps (line spacing > spot size). Applies to raster mapping only.

carrierGasFlowRate.title: Carrier Gas and Flow Rate
carrierGasFlowRate.description: Gas used to transport ablated aerosol from the ablation cell to the ICP-MS torch, with the protocol-registered target flow rate(s). Helium is standard for most UV laser systems due to superior aerosol transport. Flow rates are protocol targets; actual session values may be adjusted within ±10% during tuning.

plasmaMakeUpGasAddition.title: Plasma / Make-up Gas Addition
plasmaMakeUpGasAddition.description: Additional gas(es) mixed into the carrier stream downstream of the ablation cell, with the protocol-registered target flow rate. Ar make-up gas is standard. Small N₂ additions can enhance sensitivity for some elements. If N₂ is not added, state "None" explicitly to distinguish from not reported.

coolantGasFlowRate.title: Coolant (Plasma) Gas Flow Rate
coolantGasFlowRate.description: Flow rate of the outer (coolant/plasma) argon gas stream that sustains the ICP plasma, in L/min. Determines plasma volume and stability. Set during initial plasma optimisation and confirmed at each session start.

auxiliaryGasFlowRate.title: Auxiliary Gas Flow Rate
auxiliaryGasFlowRate.description: Flow rate of the intermediate (auxiliary) argon gas stream that positions the plasma relative to the load coil, in L/min. Affects ion extraction efficiency and oxide production rates. Distinct from the carrier gas (which transports ablation aerosol) and the coolant (plasma) gas.

rfPower.title: RF Power
rfPower.description: ICP radiofrequency forward power in watts. Fixed in the protocol; cannot be changed by analysts without defining a new protocol, because RF power affects plasma temperature, ionisation efficiency, oxide formation, and whether cool or normal plasma conditions are in effect.

signalSmoothing.title: Signal Smoothing
signalSmoothing.description: Description of any signal smoothing device or approach installed between the ablation cell and the ICP-MS to reduce pulse-to-pulse signal variability. Note: active signal smoothing devices (e.g., squid, SCFAST) are generally incompatible with high-resolution raster mapping because they degrade spatial resolution by mixing aerosol from successive laser shots. For mapping analyses, report "None" explicitly.

icPlasmaTuning.title: ICP Tuning
icPlasmaTuning.description: Description of the approach used to optimise ICP plasma conditions prior to analysis, including the reference material used for tuning and the acceptance criteria (e.g., oxide production threshold, sensitivity targets, mass calibration).

doublyChargedSpeciesMonitor.title: Doubly-Charged Species Monitor
doublyChargedSpeciesMonitor.description: The mass ratio monitored to estimate doubly-charged ion (M²⁺) formation during instrument tuning. Doubly-charged ions appear at half the mass of the parent ion and can cause isobaric interferences on analytes in that mass region. The monitor species and the mass positions monitored should be stated explicitly. Analogous to Oxide Production Method and Threshold for oxide monitoring.

doublyChargedSpeciesProduction.title: Doubly-Charged Species Production
doublyChargedSpeciesProduction.description: Measured percentage of doubly-charged ion production for the monitored species at the time of instrument tuning. The protocol should specify the acceptable threshold (e.g., <1%, <3%); the measured value for each session is recorded here. Report both the threshold and the measured value where possible.

analysisSequence.title: Analysis Sequence
analysisSequence.description: Repeating order of primary calibration standard(s), quality control standard(s), and unknown analyses within a measurement session. Editable to allow minor adjustments while maintaining the bracketing strategy defined in the protocol.

collisionGasFlowRate.title: Collision Gas Flow Rate
collisionGasFlowRate.description: Flow rate of the collision gas (typically He) introduced into the collision/reaction cell, in mL/min. Controls the degree of ion thermalization and KED efficiency. Record 'None' if the CRC is in STD mode.

cellExitDiscriminationVoltage.title: Cell Exit Discrimination Voltage
cellExitDiscriminationVoltage.description: Bias voltage applied at the collision/reaction cell exit to discriminate between analyte ions and low-energy polyatomic interferences in KED mode, in volts (V). A negative bias preferentially retards slow polyatomic ions while transmitting faster analyte ions. Record 'None' if the CRC is in STD mode.

reactionGasFlowRate.title: Reaction Gas Flow Rate
reactionGasFlowRate.description: Flow rate of the reactive gas introduced into the dynamic reaction cell (DRC), in mL/min.

dwellTime.title: Dwell Time per Mass
dwellTime.description: Count time (dwell time) per mass position for each measured isotope in milliseconds. Longer dwell times improve counting statistics and lower detection limits but reduce the number of isotopes measurable within a given scan cycle time. For mapping, scan cycle time directly determines spatial resolution at a given scan speed: shorter cycle time = finer spatial resolution.

backgroundCountTime.title: Background Count Time
backgroundCountTime.description: Total time spent measuring gas blank (background signal with laser off or shutter closed) before each ablation event, in seconds. For spot and transect analysis, a discrete background interval is measured before each ablation. For mapping, background is typically measured once per raster line or at the start of a map session rather than before each individual pixel. Editable to allow session-specific adjustment.

outlierFiltering.title: Spike / Outlier Filtering Approach
outlierFiltering.description: Method used to identify and remove anomalous signal spikes arising from micronuggets, inclusions, cracks, or instrument artifacts during time-resolved signal processing. Editable because the specific implementation may vary between sessions while remaining within the protocol framework.

nonlinearResponseCorrection.title: Pulse/Analog Detector Nonlinearity Correction
nonlinearResponseCorrection.description: Whether a correction was applied for nonlinear response at the transition between pulse-counting and analog detector modes.

memoryEffectMitigation.title: Memory Effect Mitigation
memoryEffectMitigation.description: Protocol applied to identify and minimise memory effects from high-concentration elements in the previous sample or standard that may contaminate subsequent analyses, or from incomplete aerosol washout between adjacent pixels in raster mapping mode. For mapping, the mitigation strategy involves controlling scan speed relative to washout time to ensure each pixel signal is sufficiently free of the preceding pixel's contribution.

postAcquisitionNormalization.title: Normalization / Standards-Based Correction
postAcquisitionNormalization.description: Any post-acquisition normalization applied to correct for systematic biases identified from secondary reference materials, or stoichiometric normalization applied per pixel in mapping. Distinct from the primary internal standard approach captured in Internal Standard Approach.

primaryCalibrationStandardName.title: Primary Calibration Standard Name
primaryCalibrationStandardName.description: Primary reference material(s) used to calibrate the instrument and convert raw signal intensities to concentrations or isotope ratios. Include material name, source institution, and citation for the accepted values used. Editable because the specific lot or certification vintage may differ between sessions while the material type remains the same.

secondaryReferenceMaterial.title: Secondary Reference Materials
secondaryReferenceMaterial.description: Quality-control reference materials analysed as unknowns alongside samples in the same session to assess accuracy and monitor drift. Include material name, source, and citation for accepted values used for comparison. Editable because selection of secondary RMs may vary across sessions.

torchType.title: Torch Type
torchType.description: Type of plasma torch installed. Injector inner diameter (typically 1.5–2.5 mm) affects aerosol transport efficiency and plasma conditions in LA-ICP-MS.

laserBeamEnergyProfile.title: Laser Beam Energy Profile
laserBeamEnergyProfile.description: Spatial energy distribution of the laser beam at the sample surface, and whether a beam homogenizer is installed. A flat-top (top-hat) profile produces more uniform ablation craters and more reproducible crater morphology than a Gaussian beam. This is a fixed hardware property of the laser system.

laserPulseDuration.title: Laser Pulse Duration
laserPulseDuration.description: Duration of each individual laser pulse, including units. Pulse duration determines the ablation regime: nanosecond (ns) pulses involve significant thermal effects and elemental fractionation; femtosecond (fs) pulses are non-thermal and substantially reduce elemental fractionation and matrix effects. This is a fixed hardware property of the laser system.

instrumentWarmUpSessionDurationLimit.title: Instrument Warm-up / Session Duration Limit
instrumentWarmUpSessionDurationLimit.description: Minimum warm-up time required after plasma ignition before analyses begin, and any maximum session duration enforced to maintain stable operating conditions. These constraints are part of the protocol and cannot be varied by the analyst.

eScanRange.title: E-scan Range
eScanRange.description: Electric scan range used for peak acquisition, expressed as percentage of the centre mass (%). Varies the accelerating voltage to cover masses in the vicinity of the set magnetic mass without re-scanning the magnet. Record 'N/A' if E-scan acquisition mode is not used.

tripleScanningMode.title: Triple Scanning Mode
tripleScanningMode.description: Whether each mass peak is scanned three times per cycle and the results averaged (Y/N). Used to reduce noise from short-term magnetic field instabilities on sector-field instruments. In LA-SF-ICP-MS, triple scanning affects the effective integration time per cycle and should be reported. Record 'N/A' if not applicable to the instrument.

reactionGasType.title: Reaction Gas Type
reactionGasType.description: Type of reactive gas introduced into the dynamic reaction cell (DRC) for interference removal through ion-molecule reactions. Common reaction gases include NH₃ (e.g., for Fe, Ca, K isotopes) and O₂ (e.g., for As, Ge). Record 'None' if DRC mode is not used.

multiRunSequentialAnalysisDesign.title: Multi-Run Sequential Analysis Design
multiRunSequentialAnalysisDesign.description: Whether the protocol uses a single acquisition pass or multiple sequential runs on the same sample location, each optimized for different analytical objectives. For multi-run designs, describe the number of runs, their purpose, key laser and instrument settings per run, and how outputs of one run feed into data reduction of another. Not applicable to raster mapping, where each spatial location is visited exactly once.

matrixOffsetCorrection.title: Matrix Offset Correction (LIEF)
matrixOffsetCorrection.description: Whether an empirical correction was applied to account for systematic differences in laser-induced elemental fractionation (LIEF) patterns between the external calibration standard and the sample matrix.

beamMode.title: Beam Mode
beamMode.description: Whether the beam was focused, defocused, or rastered over an area.

acceleratingVoltage.title: Accelerating Voltage
acceleratingVoltage.description: Electron beam accelerating voltage in kilovolts (kV).

beamDiameter.title: Beam Diameter
beamDiameter.description: Diameter of the focused or defocused electron beam in micrometers.

beamRasterDimensions.title: Beam Raster Dimensions
beamRasterDimensions.description: X × Y dimensions of beam raster area in micrometers, if beam raster mode was used.

beamDamageMinimization.title: Beam Damage Minimization
beamDamageMinimization.description: Description of the approach used to minimize beam damage, especially Na- and K-loss in glasses, micas, and hydrous minerals.

driftCorrection.title: Drift Correction
driftCorrection.description: Describe method used to monitor and correct for instrument drift

halogenCorrectionOnOxygen.title: Halogen Correction on Oxygen
halogenCorrectionOnOxygen.description: Whether a halogen correction was applied to calculate oxygen content by stoichiometry in halogen-bearing phases.

wdsDeadTimeCorrection.title: WDS Dead Time Correction
wdsDeadTimeCorrection.description: Method used to correct WDS proportional counter dead time at high count rates.

edsSpectralProcessingType.title: EDS Spectral Processing Type
edsSpectralProcessingType.description: Method used to process EDS spectra and extract net peak intensities.
